title: Josephus
lead: The Jewish priest and general turned Roman client who wrote the Jewish War, the Antiquities, the Life and Against Apion. His Jewish War is the main Jewish account of the war against Rome that Tacitus's Histories also covers.

sections.b: Wikipedia gives Josephus as born in Jerusalem about AD 36 or 37 and dead about 100. He governed Galilee at the start of the revolt, held out at Jotapata until it fell in 67, said he had a revelation that Vespasian would become emperor, and was released in 69. He took the name Flavius from his patrons, joined Titus's train and wrote under Flavian patronage: the Jewish War (about 75), the Antiquities (about 94), the Life and Against Apion.

Josephus covers the civil wars of 69 in a few lines and says he leaves them out because they are well known and many Greek and Roman authors describe them (Jewish War 4.9.2, in Whiston's translation). Tacitus tells at length what Josephus passes over; Josephus tells the war in Judea that Tacitus takes up in Book 5.
